peerSolutions.title: Pattern 13 printed row by row in Python
peerSolutions.author: Aman Yadav
peerSolutions.content:
Every row has one more number than the row before it. A single variable keeps the next number to print, and it is not reset when a new row starts.

The method only prints the result, as required by the template.

```python
class Solution:
    def pattern13(self, n):
        next_value = 1

        for row in range(1, n + 1):
            numbers = []
            for _ in range(row):
                numbers.append(str(next_value))
                next_value += 1
            print(" ".join(numbers))
```

The list for one row is useful here because it avoids an extra space at the end of each line. If `n` is zero or negative, no row is created.

Time complexity: `O(n^2)`. Space complexity: `O(n)` for the largest row stored before printing.
